# KM-175 — Aiur adapter integration doc

**Lane:** events · **Complexity:** 1 · **Model:** codex · **Depends on:** KM-170, KM-171, KM-173 · **Serializes with:** none
**Plan context (pinned):** [M1 plan](https://github.com/aiur-team/khala/blob/reset/m1-external-plan/docs/plans/2026-10-01-002-refactor-external-m1-thin-path-plan.md) · [contracts](https://github.com/aiur-team/khala/blob/reset/m1-external-plan/docs/build/m1/contracts.md) · [roster and graph](https://github.com/aiur-team/khala/blob/reset/m1-external-plan/docs/build/m1/roster.md) · [events plan](https://github.com/aiur-team/khala/blob/reset/m1-external-plan/docs/plans/2026-10-01-003-feat-channel-events-plan.md)
**Exclusive write surfaces:** `docs/integrations/aiur-channel-events.md`

## Outcome

One doc that makes "add Khala to Aiur" a configuration task: which Aiur topics to forward, how each maps to a Khala channel event, how dedup keys line up, how an Aiur agent posts an event today, and what a future process-level adapter needs. Every example uses a real KM-171 fixture.

## Context and evidence

- Events plan unit **E-U6** (R10; AE1). The plan file path `docs/integrations/aiur-channel-events.md` is kept (`docs/integrations/` does not exist at `5db209cc`; create it).
- **Change from the plan's recommendation.** The plan recommends Option A: an Aiur-side subscriber that runs `khala event --from-aiur - --channel <id> --ticket-prefix AIUR-`. There is no `khala event` CLI (Executor decision, reconciliation A6; contracts C7: "Only the `khala_event` MCP tool exists"), because a separate process cannot send as the agent's in-memory, process-lifetime Matrix device (M1 KTD1, contracts C4/C5) and M1 KTD7 forbids extra CLI subcommands. So this doc makes **Option B** (agent-forwarded via the `khala_event` tool) the supported path, and describes Option A as future work with its prerequisite.
- Aiur facts to cite (read-only, `/home/everdred/github/everdred/aiur/src/lib/aiur/`, commit `0972f0297`):
  - Topic set: `executor_bindings.ex:23-33` (PR, CI, attention, `agent.paused`, `branch.push`).
  - Agent `emit_event` vocabulary: `codex/dynamic_tool/emit_event.ex:12-53`; topic and payload: `agent_runner/tool_executor.ex:355-372`.
  - Dedup keys: `events/github_keys.ex:43-46,98-102`; `orchestrator/ci_lifecycle.ex:1650-1653`.
  - Self-loop and tracked-ticket filtering happen upstream in Aiur (`events/publisher.ex`, `events/sanitizer.ex:136-143`).
  - Progress emit cap 2 per turn: `codex/dynamic_tool/emit_event.ex:55`.

## Contract and invariants

contracts.md C9, verbatim: "Defined by `docs/plans/2026-10-01-003-feat-channel-events-plan.md`, with Matrix type `com.khala.event.v1`. Its contract file is `packages/contracts/src/m1/channel-event.ts`."

contracts.md C7, verbatim (the tool row the doc documents):

> | `khala_event` | `{ event?: object, aiur?: object, ticketPrefix?: string (0..16) }`, exactly one of `event` / `aiur` | `{ eventId }` or `{ skipped: true }`. Errors: `invalid_event` (with `path`, `code`), `not_connected`, `send_failed` |

The doc must state these invariants plainly: Khala never depends on Aiur at build or run time; events carry a summary only, never comment bodies, CI logs or CI instructions; attribution is always the Matrix sender, `actor` is a display hint; events never wake agents in this version; Khala credentials live with the emitting agent session, never in Aiur.

## Implementation pointers

### Files

- Create `docs/integrations/aiur-channel-events.md`.

### Worked example (doc section "Example: review requested")

````markdown
An Aiur worker has just moved PR #412 to ready for review. Aiur publishes
`ticket.395.pr.ready_for_review` (fixture: `packages/contracts/fixtures/aiur-events/pr-ready-for-review.json`).
The worker forwards it:

```json
{ "tool": "khala_event", "arguments": { "aiur": { "id": 88123, "topic": "ticket.395.pr.ready_for_review", "...": "..." }, "ticketPrefix": "AIUR-" } }
```

Both humans see one pill: `AIUR-395 review requested · feat/events-cursor · 10:09`.
A retry, or a second agent forwarding the same event, adds nothing: both derive
`key = pr:aiur-team/aiur:ready_for_review:412:3f9c2ab0d1`.
````

### Steps

1. Write the doc with these sections, in order:
   1. **What this is** — two sentences; link the events plan.
   2. **Event shape** — the C9 schema table (copy from the events plan, "Channel event schema"), and the Matrix type `com.khala.event.v1`.
   3. **Field mapping** — the events plan mapping table, corrected per KM-171: PR number for review comments comes from `comment.pull_request_url`; comment and CI `message` fields are never copied; wake records map by their `topic`. Each row names its KM-171 fixture file.
   4. **Dedup keys** — the four KTD5 forms beside the Aiur key each mirrors (cite the lines above).
   5. **Option B (supported now): agent forwarding** — after an Aiur worker's own `emit_event`, or on seeing a PR/CI event, it calls `khala_event { aiur: <event>, ticketPrefix: "AIUR-" }`. Include the worked example. Note the Aiur progress cap (2 per turn) and that `system.*` / `executor.*` topics return `{ skipped: true }`.
   6. **Option A (future): process-level adapter** — subscriber bound to `ticket.*.pr.opened`, `ticket.*.pr.ready_for_review`, `ticket.*.pr.merged`, `ticket.*.pr.parked_ready`, `ticket.*.ci.passed`, `ticket.*.ci.failed`, `ticket.*.agent.attention.*` (= `executor_bindings.ex:23-33` minus `branch.push`, which is noisy and off by default). State the prerequisite: a Khala emitter with its own long-lived device (or an outbox hand-off to a live agent session). Neither exists in M1; this needs a Khala decision first.
   7. **Safety** — the invariants above; Aiur's tracked-ticket and self-loop filters still apply upstream.
   8. **Open questions** — copy events plan Open Questions 1, 2, 4, 5, 6 with their defaults.
2. Check every path and `file:line` you cite exists (Khala paths in this repo, Aiur paths read-only).

## Test scenarios

Docs only; no automated tests. Review checks:
1. Every fixture named in the mapping table exists in `packages/contracts/fixtures/aiur-events/`.
2. The worked-example line equals KM-171's AE1 assertion.
3. No instruction tells Aiur to store Khala credentials or to import Khala code.

## Verification

```
test -f docs/integrations/aiur-channel-events.md
/bin/ls packages/contracts/fixtures/aiur-events/
pnpm --filter @khala/contracts test -- from-aiur
```

Done when the doc exists with the eight sections, every cited fixture is present, and the KM-171 tests (which prove the worked example) pass.
